meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_2H_2306). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK CONFIRMED: 2F q17-q28 = 2H q1-q12, twelve questions worth 40 marks. Coded in the same sitting as IGCSE-JUN23-F-P2.

q16 is the FIRST sighting of direct_proportion in the whole corpus, and it settles the one tier question left open in docs/audit/25-igcse-4ma1-delta.md section 3. direct_proportion and inverse_proportion had appeared on no coded paper at either tier, so the spec's split (algebraic proportion at Higher, ratio word problems at Foundation) could not be acted on. Here it is, on a HIGHER paper, given as a graph and wanted as a formula — exactly spec 2.5's 'relate algebraic solutions to graphical representation'. Both skills are currently Foundation in data/courses.ts, inherited from the GCSE list.

q14(b) is the FIRST sighting of circle_theorem_same_segment. q14(a) is the angle in a semicircle, tagged circle_theorem_angle_at_centre — the app has no separate node for it and spec 4.6 C(ii) files it with the angle-at-centre family.
q18 tagged sketching_functions with trig_graphs: three equations matched to sketches, one of them y = sin x.

q24 tagged perpendicular_gradients and understanding_straight_line_graphs: the kite's diagonal is its line of symmetry, so the fourth vertex is found by dropping a perpendicular from B onto AC and continuing an equal distance. reflections is the geometric description but costs 7, including Function Machines.
q22 needs the triangle's third angle before any elevation can be found, hence cosine_rule leading trigonometry_missing_angles.
